summary.title: Pyramid or Crab? Find a testing strategy that fits
summary.one_liner: You learn how the test pyramid, its adaptations (diamond, honeycomb, trophy) and the ice cone and crab shapes combine unit, integration, E2E, static and visual tests into a strategy that fits your project and users.
keywords: how to choose a testing strategy
how many unit tests to write
takeaways: The test pyramid (unit, integration, E2E) ranks tests by cost and confidence; higher layers give more confidence but cost more and should be fewer.
Adaptations such as the test diamond, testing honeycomb (for microservices) and testing trophy (adds static analysis) shift emphasis toward integration tests.
The ice cone is an anti-pattern with heavy manual and UI testing; the crab emphasizes E2E and visual testing and can suit smaller projects.
Define your testing goal around serving users rather than chasing 100% coverage, and choose a strategy that fits your architecture and requirements.
summary.summary: The article is the second part of a web.dev testing series and explains how to combine testing types into a strategy. It starts with testing goals, arguing that tests should resemble real user behaviour rather than maximise coverage. It then walks through the classic test pyramid by Mike Cohn and Martin Fowler, followed by adaptations: the test diamond, Spotify's testing honeycomb for microservices, and Kent C. Dodds' testing trophy that adds static analysis. It closes with UI-heavy shapes, the ice cone (anti-pattern) and the testing crab, and gives practical advice that the right strategy depends on the application.
